Old receive and send timeout numbers and the detach-filter number aliased by detach-BPF are not in these fragments.
New stamp ioctl numbers beyond the OLD timeval and timespec forms are not shown.
Termios ioctl numbers, line-discipline behaviour and window-size update semantics are not shown.

findings.text: The routed headers publish user-visible ABI for sockets, socket ioctls, filesystem statistics, terminal control and DRM management, intended for shared use by kernel and user code through stable numeric identifiers and record layouts.

Socket options SO_NOFCS is 43, SO_LOCK_FILTER is 44, SO_SELECT_ERR_QUEUE is 45, SO_BUSY_POLL is 46, SO_MAX_PACING_RATE is 47, SO_BPF_EXTENSIONS is 48, SO_INCOMING_CPU is 49, SO_ATTACH_BPF is 50, SO_ATTACH_REUSEPORT_CBPF is 51 and SO_ATTACH_REUSEPORT_EBPF is 52, while SO_DETACH_BPF aliases the detach-filter option defined elsewhere.

Further socket options continue sequentially with SO_CNX_ADVICE 53, SCM_TIMESTAMPING_OPT_STATS 54, SO_MEMINFO 55, SO_INCOMING_NAPI_ID 56, SO_COOKIE 57, SCM_TIMESTAMPING_PKTINFO 58, SO_PEERGROUPS 59, SO_ZEROCOPY 60, SO_TXTIME 61 with SCM_TXTIME sharing that value, and SO_BINDTOIFINDEX 62.

Legacy time options use SO_TIMESTAMP_OLD 29 with nanosecond and full timestamping companions 35 and 37, while time64-ready replacements use SO_TIMESTAMP_NEW 63, SO_TIMESTAMPNS_NEW 64, SO_TIMESTAMPING_NEW 65, SO_RCVTIMEO_NEW 66 and SO_SNDTIMEO_NEW 67.

Higher socket options assign SO_DETACH_REUSEPORT_BPF 68, SO_PREFER_BUSY_POLL 69, SO_BUSY_POLL_BUDGET 70, SO_NETNS_COOKIE 71, SO_BUF_LOCK 72, SO_RESERVE_MEM 73, SO_TXREHASH 74, SO_RCVMARK 75, SO_PASSPIDFD 76, SO_PEERPIDFD 77, SO_DEVMEM_LINEAR 78 with matching SCM name, SO_DEVMEM_DMABUF 79 with matching SCM name, SO_DEVMEM_DONTNEED 80, SCM_TS_OPT_ID 81, SO_RCVPRIORITY 82, SO_PASSRIGHTS 83, SO_INQ 84 with SCM_INQ sharing it, and SO_RIGHTS_NOTRUNC 85.

Public names SO_TIMESTAMP, SO_TIMESTAMPNS, SO_TIMESTAMPING, SO_RCVTIMEO and SO_SNDTIMEO resolve either statically to their OLD companions or dynamically by comparing the sizes of time_t and kernel long, selecting OLD when equal and NEW otherwise; SCM_TIMESTAMP family aliases the resolved SO names.

Socket ioctl numbers use FIOSETOWN 0x8901, SIOCSPGRP 0x8902, FIOGETOWN 0x8903, SIOCGPGRP 0x8904, SIOCATMARK 0x8905, SIOCGSTAMP_OLD 0x8906 for timeval stamps and SIOCGSTAMPNS_OLD 0x8907 for timespec stamps.

The statfs word type adapts to architecture, naming kernel long on 64-bit ABIs and 32-bit unsigned otherwise, and packing macros ARCH_PACK_STATFS64 and ARCH_PACK_COMPAT_STATFS64 allow per-arch alignment control, defaulting to empty when not overridden.

The statfs record holds filesystem type, block size, total blocks, free blocks, available blocks, total inodes, free inodes, filesystem identifier, maximum name length, fragment size, mount flags and four spare words, in that order.

The 64-bit variants keep type, block size and identifier plus name length, fragment size, flags and spares as words but widen block and inode counts to 64-bit; compat_statfs64 fixes the word-sized members to 32-bit unsigned for cross-ABI use.
Generic byteswap declares 64-bit operations implemented through 32-bit steps, and each uapi header defines its own include guard macro to ensure single inclusion.
Terminal code uses cc_t as unsigned char for control characters, speed_t as unsigned int for baud rates and tcflag_t as unsigned int for mode bitfields.

Input modes define IGNBRK 1, BRKINT 2, IGNPAR 4, PARMRK 8, INPCK 16, ISTRIP 32, INLCR 64, IGNCR 128, ICRNL 256 and IXANY 2048, controlling break handling, parity handling, stripping, newline translation and restart behaviour.

Additional input modes add IUCLC 512, IXON 1024, IXOFF 4096, IMAXBEL 8192 and IUTF8 16384 for case handling, software flow control, bell behaviour and UTF-8 mode; output processing uses OPOST 1 with OCRNL 8, ONOCR 16, ONLRET 32, OFILL 64, OFDEL 128, OLCUC 2 and ONLCR 4.

Output delay masks group newline, carriage-return, tab, backspace, vertical-tab and form-feed handling with NLDLY 256, CRDLY 1536, TABDLY 6144, BSDLY 8192, VTDLY 16384 and FFDLY 32768, each offering zero plus one or more stepped values and XTABS equal to TAB3.

Classic baud identifiers B0 through B38400 encode 0 through 15, with EXTA matching B19200 and EXTB matching B38400; high control bits provide ADDRB, CMSPAR for stick parity and CRTSCTS for hardware flow, and IBSHIFT 16 separates input baud from output baud.

Control flags define CBAUD mask 0x100f, CSIZE mask 48 with CS5 through CS8 stepping by 16, CSTOPB 64, CREAD 128, PARENB 256, PARODD 512, HUPCL 1024, CLOCAL 2048, CBAUDEX and BOTHER both 4096, extended rates B57600 through B4000000 as 0x1001 through 0x100f, and CIBAUD mask 0x100f0000.

Queue control uses TCOOFF 0, TCOON 1, TCIOFF 2 and TCION 3 for output suspension and start-stop signalling, TCIFLUSH 0, TCOFLUSH 1 and TCIOFLUSH 2 for discarding queued data, and TCSANOW 0, TCSADRAIN 1 and TCSAFLUSH 2 for when termios changes take effect.

Termios structures store input, output, control and local flags followed by line discipline, a fixed control-character array and, for termios2 and ktermios only, input and output speeds; plain termios omits the speeds while the larger forms append them.

Control-character slots number VINTR 0 through VEOL2 16 in order VINTR, VQUIT, VERASE, VKILL, VEOF, VTIME, VMIN, VSWTC, VSTART, VSTOP, VSUSP, VEOL, VREPRINT, VDISCARD, VWERASE, VLNEXT and VEOL2, with array size NCCS 19 leaving spare entries.

Local modes assign ISIG 1, ICANON 2, XCASE 4, ECHO 8, ECHOE 16, ECHOK 32, ECHONL 64, NOFLSH 128, TOSTOP 256, ECHOCTL 512, ECHOPRT 1024, ECHOKE 2048, FLUSHO 4096, PENDIN 16384, IEXTEN 32768 and EXTPROC 65536 for signal, canonical, echo and extension behaviour.

Window size carries row, column and pixel width and height as unsigned short in that order; legacy termio mirrors termios with short-sized flags, a char line discipline and eight control characters indicated by NCC 8.
Modem status bits define LE 1, DTR 2, RTS 4, ST 8, SR 16, CTS 32, CAR 64, RNG 128, DSR 256, OUT1 8192, OUT2 16384 and LOOP 32768, with CD sharing CAR value and RI sharing RNG value.

The generic user context links flags, a pointer to the next context, the signal stack, the machine register state and finally the signal mask, keeping the mask last so the record can grow without moving earlier fields.

DRM core declares driver name drm, minimum allocation order 5, maximum order 22 and lockable RAM percentage 10; context, drawable and magic handles are unsigned int, while the generic handle type appears as unsigned int in two configurations and unsigned long with explicit 8 to 64-bit fixed-width aliases plus size type in another.

Hardware lock words reserve held bit 0x80000000 and contended bit 0x40000000 with helpers to test each and to extract the owning context; control operations enumerate add, remove, install-handler and uninstall-handler with an IRQ field; map types span framebuffer, registers, shared memory, AGP, scatter-gather and consistent memory as 0 through 5.

Mapping flags mark restricted, read-only, locked, kernel, write-combining, contains-lock, removable and driver-managed as powers of two from 1 to 128; lock control offers ready, quiescent, flush, flush-all and two halt-queue variants; DMA dispatch and request flags provide block, while-locked, priority, wait, smaller-ok and larger-ok semantics.

Drawing support pairs a four-short clip rectangle with a count plus pointer to rectangles; texture regions chain through next and previous indices with use flag, padding and age; version and unique records follow a length plus user-buffer pattern for name, date, description and driver instance strings.

The hardware lock record keeps a volatile unsigned lock word padded to 64 bytes to occupy a full cache line, and acquisition requests pair a context identifier with ready, quiescent, flush or halt modifiers that order DMA draining before the lock is granted.

Memory maps describe offset, size, type, flags, handle for mmap or kernel address and MTRR slot, with a helper binding a context to a private handle; client records carry index, authentication state, process and user identifiers, magic and ioctl count; statistics hold a count plus fifteen value-and-type pairs covering locks, opens, ioctls, IRQs and DMA categories; buffer management uses descriptor counts with low and high watermarks and placement flags, plus info, free-list, publication and mapping records that exchange user pointers to lists and virtual areas.

Several DRM records carry user-space pointers and separate lengths that require validation and bounded copying, the lock word relies on volatile shared-memory semantics with explicit contention bits, and time-dependent socket and ioctl numbers have OLD and NEW variants whose misuse truncates timestamps or misroutes control operations.
